Agentic Onion Sellers

"Ze finest recommendations, smuggled past ze checkpoint in a string of onions." Which models to use on GitHub Copilot, OpenCode Go, OpenCode Zen and ClinePass, per kind of task — recomputed daily from provider pricing and Artificial Analysis benchmarks.

Setting ze tables…

Score is quality minus a penalty for each doubling of cost above $1 per task and of response time above 60 s, all in index points. Quality is the category's mix of Artificial Analysis indexes. Each model is listed at its best-scoring reasoning effort, shown after its name. $/task is what one Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index task would cost at the provider's prices, so it accounts for how many tokens a model spends; Time is seconds until a 500-token answer is complete, thinking included; $/1M is the blended per-token price (3 output tokens per input token). Pricing: GitHub Copilot docs, OpenCode Go docs, OpenCode Zen docs, ClinePass docs. Benchmarks: Artificial Analysis. Source: KuzniAI/onion-sellers. Inspired by René's onion-selling disguise in 'Allo 'Allo!.

A model at $1 per task and 60 s scores exactly its quality, and every number is in index points, so the two rates read as exchange rates: how many quality points a model may give up to be half the price or twice as fast. Nothing is normalized against the other candidates, so one provider's lineup never moves another model's score. quality is a per-category mix (weights sum to 1) of four Artificial Analysis indexes in raw points: intelligenceIndex, engineeringIndex, financeAndAccountingIndex and strategyAndOpsIndex. The indexes are not on a common scale -- strategyAndOpsIndex runs high for cheap models -- so keep its weight at 0.4 or lower. engineeringIndex tracks intelligenceIndex almost exactly (r=0.995), so mixing those two states intent more than it changes rankings. Cost per task = AA's measured cost to run one Intelligence Index task x (provider blended price / AA blended price), blended at 3 output tokens per input token; it prices in how many tokens a model actually spends, not just its per-token price. Per-token pricing is a documented simplification, since Copilot (plan + credits), OpenCode Go and ClinePass (flat plans with caps) aren't billed per token; plan caps are not scored. Response time = mean time to first answer token + 500 / mean output tokens per second, from performance_v3 (the older performance block returns null from 2026-12-10); it includes thinking time, which tokens per second alone hides. costFloorPerTask and responseTimeFloorSeconds mean 'cheap enough' and 'fast enough': anything below them earns no further credit, otherwise a near-useless model that costs almost nothing would win on a log scale. Every Artificial Analysis reasoning-effort variant of a mapped model (Low ... Max) is scored as its own candidate at the provider's price, and each model is listed once per category at its best-scoring effort. - The title.
- A paragraph in Allo Allo voice ("Listen very carefully, I shall say zis only once…") saying what the site is.
